entities.summary: Hōjō Tokimasa  was a Japanese samurai lord who was the first shikken (regent) of the Kamakura shogunate and head of the Hōjō clan. He was shikken from 1203 until his abdication in 1205, and Protector of Kyoto from 1185 to 1186.

entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hōjō Tokimasa (1138–1215), a pivotal figure in early medieval Japan, was the architect behind the Hōjō clan's ascent to power and the first *shikken* (regent) of the Kamakura shogunate. His shrewd political maneuvering transformed a nascent military government into a lasting institution, effectively shifting Japan's political center from the imperial court in Kyoto to the samurai stronghold in Kamakura. Tokimasa’s strategic marriage of his daughter, Hōjō Masako, to Minamoto no Yoritomo, the future founder of the shogunate, laid the foundational stone for his family's unprecedented influence, making him a critical player in the Genpei War and the subsequent establishment of samurai rule.

Following Minamoto no Yoritomo's death in 1199, Tokimasa systematically consolidated his family's authority. He navigated the turbulent succession of Yoritomo's sons, Minamoto no Yoriie and Minamoto no Sanetomo, ultimately sidelining or eliminating rival factions within the shogunate. By 1203, he formally assumed the title of *shikken*, a position initially conceived as a temporary regency but which he molded into the de facto supreme executive office, effectively governing Japan on behalf of the Minamoto shoguns. His short tenure as *shikken* until 1205 was marked by decisive actions to neutralize opposition, including the forced abdication and later assassination of his grandson, Yoriie, and the suppression of the Hiki clan, solidifying the Hōjō's grip on power.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hōjō Tokimasa established the *shikken* regency, fundamentally transforming the Kamakura Shogunate into a Hōjō-dominated entity that governed Japan for over a century. His actions solidified the shift of political power from the imperial court to the samurai class.
